pack.title: Daily Stack
pack.description: Eight mixed discoveries, rotating with your local date.

categories.title: WAYS TO COOK EGGS
categories.triviaFact: Poaching cooks an egg in liquid without its shell.

categories.title: CIRCUS PERFORMERS
categories.triviaFact: An aerialist performs acrobatics above the ground using suspended equipment.

categories.title: PIANO COMPONENTS
categories.triviaFact: A piano damper stops a string from vibrating when it rests against it.

categories.title: BEFORE WALK
categories.triviaFact: A spacewalk takes an astronaut outside a spacecraft while in space.

redHerrings.note: TIGHTROPE suggests the circus, but is not a performer; CAKE, CAT and SPACE all join it in making WALK words.

categories.title: CULINARY SPICES
categories.triviaFact: Saffron consists of the dried stigmas of a particular crocus flower.

categories.title: WEATHER INSTRUMENTS
categories.triviaFact: A barometer measures air pressure, helping observers track changes in the weather.

categories.title: BALLET MOVEMENTS AND POSES
categories.triviaFact: A pirouette is a turn performed while balancing on one leg.

categories.title: BEFORE MILL
categories.triviaFact: A treadmill once used human or animal movement to drive machinery.

redHerrings.note: PEPPER would make a convincing fifth spice, but it is needed to complete PEPPER MILL, WINDMILL, TREADMILL and SAWMILL.

categories.title: OPEN LANDSCAPES
categories.triviaFact: Permafrost lies beneath much of the Arctic tundra.

categories.title: ORCHESTRAL SOUND MAKERS
categories.triviaFact: Timpani can be tuned to different pitches by adjusting the tension of their drumheads.

categories.title: WALLET CONTENTS
categories.triviaFact: A receipt records a transaction and can serve as proof of purchase.

categories.title: FOLLOW GREEN
categories.triviaFact: Greenhorn describes an inexperienced person rather than a literal horn.

redHerrings.note: HORN tempts a fifth orchestral instrument, but ROOM, HOUSE and LIGHT all need it to complete the GREEN expressions.

categories.title: WILD CATS
categories.triviaFact: A lynx has ear tufts and broad paws that help it travel over snow.

categories.title: CAR BRANDS
categories.triviaFact: Volvo's name comes from Latin and means I roll.

categories.title: GEOMETRIC SOLIDS
categories.triviaFact: A cylinder has two parallel circular bases connected by a curved surface.

categories.title: BEFORE CAKE
categories.triviaFact: Sponge cake gets its light texture from air incorporated into the mixture.

redHerrings.note: JAGUAR could make a fifth wild cat, but LOTUS, TESLA and VOLVO need it to form the four car brands.

categories.title: USED TO KEEP TIME
categories.triviaFact: A sundial uses the changing position of a shadow to indicate the time of day.

categories.title: ANIMALS THAT BUILD HOMES
categories.triviaFact: Weaver birds tie and weave plant fibers into elaborate nests.

categories.title: BRITISH MUSICAL NOTE NAMES
categories.triviaFact: A breve lasts twice as long as a semibreve in standard musical notation.

categories.title: FOLLOW STOP
categories.triviaFact: Stop-motion animation creates movement from photographs of objects moved in small steps.

redHerrings.note: WATCH would fit beside CLOCK and SUNDIAL, but STOPWATCH, STOP SIGN, STOPGAP and STOP MOTION form the intended fourth group.

categories.title: CHEESES
categories.triviaFact: Feta is traditionally made from sheep's milk or a mixture of sheep's and goat's milk.

categories.title: FIVE-LETTER COUNTRIES
categories.triviaFact: Nepal's national flag has two triangular sections rather than a rectangular outline.

categories.title: ENGLISH WORDS FROM JAPANESE
categories.triviaFact: Origami combines Japanese words associated with folding and paper.

categories.title: ANAGRAMS OF EAST
categories.triviaFact: Anagrams preserve the count of each letter even when the arrangement changes.

redHerrings.note: CHILE can name a pepper, tempting a food connection with the cheeses, but NEPAL, SPAIN and EGYPT make its country group precise.

categories.title: FENCING VOCABULARY
categories.triviaFact: A parry deflects an opponent's blade to prevent an attack from landing.

categories.title: FLIGHTLESS BIRDS
categories.triviaFact: Penguin wings have evolved into flippers that propel the birds underwater.

categories.title: MAP PROJECTIONS
categories.triviaFact: A map projection converts positions on a curved surface into a flat representation.

categories.title: VERBS FOR OBSTRUCTING
categories.triviaFact: Foil can mean to prevent a plan from succeeding as well as naming a fencing weapon.

redHerrings.note: FOIL is a fencing weapon, but FRUSTRATE, HINDER and BLOCK require its verb meaning to complete their connection.

categories.title: POLYGONS WITH AT LEAST SIX SIDES
categories.triviaFact: A nonagon has nine sides, while a decagon has ten.

categories.title: VISUAL PHENOMENA
categories.triviaFact: Parallax is a change in an object's apparent position when the viewpoint changes.

categories.title: BIRD NAMES THAT ARE ALSO VERBS
categories.triviaFact: To hawk something is to offer it for sale, while to crow can mean to boast.

categories.title: REVERSE TO MAKE A DIFFERENT WORD
categories.triviaFact: Reversing STRESSED produces DESSERTS, turning a feeling into something sweet.

redHerrings.note: RAIL reverses to LIAR, so it tempts the reversal set; only RAIL also names a bird and a verb, completing that group.
